Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১) Which time frame is called Elizabethan Period in English Literature?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Elizabethan Period started when the Queen Elizabeth crowned which was at 1558 and continued till her death at 1603. Elizabeth I, bynames the Virgin Queen and Good Queen Bess, (born September 7, 1533, Greenwich, near London, England—died March 24, 1603, Richmond, Surrey), queen of England (1558–1603) during a period, often called the Elizabethan Age. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Elizabeth-I

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২) Which one is the oldest English Literary period?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: The oldest English Literary period is The Anglo-Saxon period. It was started at 450 A.D and lasted till 1066 A.D. It is also the longest English literary period in the context of duration. Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ৩) The Renaissance English literary period is divided into ___ division.
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: The Renaissance English literary period is divided into 4 division. Elizabethan period, Jacobean period, Caroline period and Commonwealth period. Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ৪) Which one is the second oldest English Literary period?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Anglo-Saxon Period is the oldest English literary period. Then Anglo-Norman period started which was the first portion of the Middle English Period. It started in 1066 A.D and ended in 1340. Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ৫) Who wrote the first English epic ‘Beowulf’?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Most of the literary works of the Anglo-Saxon period are written by anonymous writer. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Beowulf

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ৬) What is the name of the evil monster/antagonist in Beowulf?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Beowulf falls into two parts. It opens in Denmark, where King Hrothgar’s splendid mead hall, Heorot, has been ravaged for 12 years by nightly visits from an evil monster, Grendel, who carries off Hrothgar’s warriors and devours them. Unexpectedly, young Beowulf, a prince of the Geats of southern Sweden, arrives with a small band of retainers and offers to cleanse Heorot of its monster. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Beowulf

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ৭) Which one is the literary features of the Anglo-Saxon period?
৮) Who is the first English historian?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: St. Bede the Venerable, Bede also spelled Baeda or Beda, (born 672/673, traditionally Monkton in Jarrow, Northumbria [England]—died May 25, 735, Jarrow; canonized 1899; feast day May 25), Anglo-Saxon theologian, historian, and chronologist. St. Bede is best known for his Historia ecclesiastica gentis Anglorum (“Ecclesiastical History of the English People”), a source vital to the history of the conversion to Christianity of the Anglo-Saxon tribes. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Saint-Bede-the-Venerable

Cynewulf known as – The writer of Christ.

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১০) ‘The Historia regum Britanniae’- a famous middle English literary period’s book was written by-
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Historia regum Britanniae, (Latin: “History of the Kings of Britain”) fictional history of Britain written by Geoffrey of Monmouth sometime between 1135 and 1139. The Historia regum Britanniae was one of the most popular books of the Middle Ages. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Historia-regum-Britanniae

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১১) Who wrote ‘Opus tertium’?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Opus majus, Opus tertium-- written by Roger bacon. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Roger-Bacon

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১২) In “The Parlement of Foules” - Geoffrey Chaucer describe the tradition of-
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: The Parlement of Foules, a 699-line poem in rhyme royal by Geoffrey Chaucer, written in 1380–90. Composed in the tradition of French romances (while at the same time questioning the merits of that tradition), this poem has been called one of the best occasional verses in the English language. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Parlement-of-Foules

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১৩) Which one is Chaucer’s literary work?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: All are written by Chaucer. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Geoffrey-Chaucer

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.option4: ঘ) The Tale of Two Cities
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: The Tale of Two Cities is a novel by Charles Dickens and the rest of the prologues are included in “The Canterbury Tales”. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Canterbury-Tales

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১৫) Who translated Bible completely for the first time into English?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: John Wycliffe, Wycliffe also spelled Wycliff, Wyclif, Wicliffe, or Wiclif, (born c. 1330, Yorkshire, England—died December 31, 1384, Lutterworth, Leicestershire), English theologian, philosopher, church reformer, and promoter of the first complete translation of the Bible into English. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/John-Wycliffe

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১৬) Who wrote famous allegorical work “Piers Plowman”?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Piers Plowman, in full The Vision of Piers Plowman, Middle English alliterative poem presumed to have been written by William Langland. Three versions of Piers Plowman are extant: A, the poem’s short early form, dating from the 1360s; B, a major revision and extension of A made in the late 1370s; and C, a less “literary” version of B dating from the 1380s and apparently intended to focus the work’s doctrinal issues. Some scholars think that version C may not be entirely attributable to Langland. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Piers-Plowman

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১৭) ‘Elizabethan Period’ is named after-
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: ‘Elizabethan Period’ is named after Queen Elizabeth-I who reigned England form 1558 to 1603. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Elizabeth-I

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১৮) Who is the main poet of Elizabethan Period?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: William Shakespeare was the main poet of Elizabethan Period.

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ১৯) ‘Utopia’-by Thomas More was originally written in-
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Utopia was originally written in Latin. Alternative Titles: “Libellus…de optimo reipublicae statu, deque nova insula Utopia”. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Utopia-by-More

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২০) The Faerie Queene- by Edmund Spencer is a famous-
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: The Faerie Queene, one of the great long poems in the English language, written in the 16th century by Edmund Spenser. As originally conceived, the poem was to have been a religious-moral-political allegory in 12 books, each consisting of the adventures of a knight representing a particular moral virtue; Book I, for example, recounts the legend of the Red Cross Knight, or Holiness. The knights serve the Faerie Queene, who represents Glory and Queen Elizabeth I. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Faerie-Queene

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২১) Who wrote first English Comedy?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Nicholas Udall, (born December 1505?, Southampton, Hampshire, Eng.—died December 1556, Westminster), English playwright, translator, and schoolmaster who wrote the first known English comedy, Ralph Roister Doister. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Nicholas-Udall

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২২) Who wrote the first English tragedy?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Gorboduc, play by Thomas Norton and Thomas Sackville that takes as its subject Gorboduc, a mythical king of ancient Britain. First performed in 1561, it is the earliest English tragic play in blank verse. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Gorboduc-by-Norton-and-Sackville

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২৩) Which one is the first revenge tragedy in English Tragedy?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: The Spanish Tragedy- is the first revenge tragedy in English literature. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Thomas-Kyd

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২৪) Who wrote criticism book- “An Apology for Poetry”?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Sir Philip Sydney wrote criticism book- “An Apology for Poetry”. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Philip-Sidney

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২৫) Which one is the first play by Cristopher Marlowe?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.option4: ঘ) Massacre of St. Bartholomew’s Day
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Tamburlaine the Great, first play by Christopher Marlowe, produced about 1587 and published in 1590. The play was written in two parts, each of which has five acts, and was based on the earlier Silva de varia lección (1540; The Foreste; or, Collection of Histories) by the early 16th-century Spanish scholar and humanist Pedro Mexía. Marlowe’s “mighty line,” as Ben Jonson called it, established blank verse as the standard for later Elizabethan and Jacobean dramatic writing. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Tamburlaine-the-Great

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২৬) ‘University Wits’ were from which university?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: The university wits include Christopher Marlowe, Robert Greene, and Thomas Nashe (all graduates of Cambridge), as well as Thomas Lodge and George Peele (both of Oxford). Another of the wits, though not university-trained, was Thomas Kyd. Preceded by John Lyly (an Oxford man), they prepared the way for William Shakespeare. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/University-Wits

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২৭) “The Arrangement of Paris”- was written by-
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: George Peele wrote “The Arrangement of Paris”. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/George-Peele

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২৮) Who is the author of - “The Unfortunate Traveller”?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: The Unfortunate Traveller is a brutal and realistic tale of adventure narrated with speed and economy. The book describes the travels through Germany and Italy of its rogue hero, Jacke Wilton. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Unfortunate-Traveller-or-The-Life-of-Jacke-Wilton

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ২৯) Who translated Homer’s “Illiad” and “Odyssey” into English?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: The first books of his translation of the Iliad appeared in 1598. It was completed in 1611, and his version of the Odyssey appeared in 1616. Chapman’s Homer contains passages of great power and beauty and inspired the sonnet of John Keats “On First Looking into Chapman’s Homer” (1815). Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Shakespeare started his literary work in 1592 and died in 1616. It is considered that the Shakespearean Age is 1590 to 1616. Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ৩৬) Shakespeare is mainly famous for his -
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: William Shakespeare, Shakespeare also spelled Shakspere, byname Bard of Avon or Swan of Avon, (baptized April 26, 1564, Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire, England—died April 23, 1616, Stratford-upon-Avon), English poet, dramatist, and actor often called the English national poet and considered by many to be the greatest dramatist of all time. Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ৪৩) Why is Shakespeare still important today?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.option1: ক) Portraying the nature in his dramas
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.option3: গ) Describing human emotions and love through characters in his plays
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Shakespeare remains vital because his plays present people and situations that we recognize today. His characters have an emotional reality that transcends time, and his plays depict familiar experiences, ranging from family squabbles to falling in love to war. The fact that his plays are performed and adapted around the world underscores the universal appeal of his storytelling. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/William-Shakespeare

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ৪৪) How many plays did Shakespeare write?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: There is some dispute about how many plays Shakespeare wrote. The general consensus is 37. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/William-Shakespeare

Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.question: ৪৫) Which one is Shakespeare’s revenge tragedy?
Writers From Old Age to Elizabethan Age.exp: Hamlet (c. 1599–1601), on the other hand, chooses a tragic model closer to that of Titus Andronicus and Kyd’s The Spanish Tragedy. In form, Hamlet is a revenge tragedy. It features characteristics found in Titus as well: a protagonist charged with the responsibility of avenging a heinous crime against the protagonist’s family, a cunning antagonist, the appearance of the ghost of the murdered person, the feigning of madness to throw off the villain’s suspicions, the play within the play as a means of testing the villain, and still more. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/William-Shakespeare/Julius-Caesar#ref232327
